studies.title: Fear conditioning in frontotemporal lobar degeneration and Alzheimer's disease.
studies.abstract: Emotional blunting and abnormal processing of rewards and punishments represent early features of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Better understanding of the physiological underpinnings of these emotional changes can be facilitated by the use of classical psychology approaches. Fear conditioning (FC) is an extensively used paradigm for studying emotional processing that has rarely been applied to the study of dementia. We studied FC in controls (n = 25), Alzheimer's disease (n = 25) and FTLD (n = 25). A neutral stimulus (coloured square on a computer screen) was repeatedly paired with a 1 s burst of 100 db white noise. Change in skin conductance response to the neutral stimulus was used to measure conditioning. Physiological-anatomical correlations were examined using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). Both patient groups showed impaired acquisition of conditioned responses. However, the basis for this deficit appeared to differ between groups. In Alzheimer's disease, impaired FC occurred despite normal electrodermal responses to the aversive stimulus. In contrast, FTLD patients showed reduced skin conductance responses to the aversive stimulus, which contributed significantly to their FC deficit. VBM identified correlations with physiological reactivity in the amygdala, anterior cingulate cortex, orbitofrontal cortex and insula. These data indicate that Alzheimer's disease and FTLD both show abnormalities in emotional learning, but they suggest that in FTLD this is associated with a deficit in basic electrodermal response to aversive stimuli, consistent with the emotional blunting described with this disorder. Deficits in responses to aversive stimuli could contribute to both the behavioural and cognitive features of FTLD and Alzheimer's disease. Further study of FC in humans and animal models of dementia could provide a valuable window into these symptoms.

studies.title: Non-Fluent Speech in Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration.
studies.abstract: We investigated the cognitive and neural bases of impaired speech fluency, a central feature of primary progressive aphasia. Speech fluency was assessed in 35 patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) who presented with progressive non-fluent aphasia (PNFA, n=11), semantic dementia (SemD, n=12), or a social and executive disorder without aphasia (SOC/EXEC, n=12). Fluency was quantified as the number of words per minute in an extended, semi-structured speech sample. This was related to language characteristics of the speech sample and to neuropsychological measures. PNFA patients were significantly less fluent than controls and other FTLD patients. Fluency correlated with grammatical expression but not with speech errors or executive difficulty. SemD and SOC/EXEC patients were also less fluent than controls. In SemD, fluency was associated with semantically limited content. In SOC/EXEC, fluency was associated with executive limitations. Voxel-based morphometry analyses of high-resolution MRI related fluency to gray matter volume in left inferior frontal, insula, and superior temporal regions for the entire cohort of FTLD patients. This region overlapped partially distinct atrophic areas in each FTLD subgroup. It thus appears to play a crucial role in speech fluency, which can be interrupted in different ways in different FTLD subgroups.

studies.title: Grey and white matter correlates of recent and remote autobiographical memory retrieval--insights from the dementias.
studies.abstract: The capacity to remember self-referential past events relies on the integrity of a distributed neural network. Controversy exists, however, regarding the involvement of specific brain structures for the retrieval of recently experienced versus more distant events. Here, we explored how characteristic patterns of atrophy in neurodegenerative disorders differentially disrupt remote versus recent autobiographical memory. Eleven behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia, 10 semantic dementia, 15 Alzheimer's disease patients and 14 healthy older Controls completed the Autobiographical Interview. All patient groups displayed significant remote memory impairments relative to Controls. Similarly, recent period retrieval was significantly compromised in behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer's disease, yet semantic dementia patients scored in line with Controls. Voxel-based morphometry and diffusion tensor imaging analyses, for all participants combined, were conducted to investigate grey and white matter correlates of remote and recent autobiographical memory retrieval. Neural correlates common to both recent and remote time periods were identified, including the hippocampus, medial prefrontal, and frontopolar cortices, and the forceps minor and left hippocampal portion of the cingulum bundle. Regions exclusively implicated in each time period were also identified. The integrity of the anterior temporal cortices was related to the retrieval of remote memories, whereas the posterior cingulate cortex emerged as a structure significantly associated with recent autobiographical memory retrieval. This study represents the first investigation of the grey and white matter correlates of remote and recent autobiographical memory retrieval in neurodegenerative disorders. Our findings demonstrate the importance of core brain structures, including the medial prefrontal cortex and hippocampus, irrespective of time period, and point towards the contribution of discrete regions in mediating successful retrieval of distant versus recently experienced events.

studies.title: Right anterior temporal lobe dysfunction underlies theory of mind impairments in semantic dementia.
studies.abstract: Semantic dementia is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the amodal and profound loss of semantic knowledge attributable to the degeneration of the left anterior temporal lobe. Although traditionally conceptualized as a language disorder, patients with semantic dementia display significant alterations in behaviour and socioemotional functioning. Recent evidence points to an impaired capacity for theory of mind in predominantly left-lateralized cases of semantic dementia; however, it remains unclear to what extent semantic impairments contribute to these deficits. Further the neuroanatomical signature of such disturbance remains unknown. Here, we sought to determine the neural correlates of theory of mind performance in patients with left predominant semantic dementia (n=11), in contrast with disease-matched cases with behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (n=10) and Alzheimer's disease (n=10), and healthy older individuals (n=14) as control participants. Participants completed a simple cartoons task, in which they were required to describe physical and theory of mind scenarios. Irrespective of subscale, patients with semantic dementia exhibited marked impairments relative to control subjects; however, only theory of mind deficits persisted when we covaried for semantic comprehension. Voxel-based morphometry analyses revealed that atrophy in right anterior temporal lobe structures, including the right temporal fusiform cortex, right inferior temporal gyrus, bilateral temporal poles and amygdalae, correlated significantly with theory of mind impairments in the semantic dementia group. Our results point to the marked disruption of cognitive functions beyond the language domain in semantic dementia, not exclusively attributable to semantic processing impairments. The significant involvement of right anterior temporal structures suggests that with disease evolution, the encroachment of pathology into the contralateral hemisphere heralds the onset of social cognitive deficits in this syndrome.

studies.title: Food knowledge depends upon the integrity of both sensory and functional properties: a VBM, TBSS and DTI tractography study.
studies.abstract: Food constitutes a fuel of life for human beings. It is therefore of chief importance that their recognition system readily identifies the most relevant properties of food by drawing on semantic memory. One of the most relevant properties to be considered is the level of processing impressed by humans on food. We hypothesized that recognition of raw food capitalizes on sensory properties and that of transformed food on functional properties, consistently with the hypothesis of a sensory-functional organization of semantic knowledge. To test this hypothesis, patients with Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, primary progressive aphasia, and healthy controls performed lexical-semantic tasks with food (raw and transformed) and non-food (living and nonliving) stimuli. Correlations between task performance and local grey matter concentration (VBM) and white matter fractional anisotropy (TBSS) led to two main findings. First, recognition of raw food and living things implicated occipital cortices, typically involved in processing sensory information and, second, recognition of processed food and nonliving things implicated the middle temporal gyrus and surrounding white matter tracts, regions that have been associated with functional properties. In conclusion, the present study confirms and extends the hypothesis of a sensory and a functional organization of semantic knowledge.

studies.title: The salience network causally influences default mode network activity during moral reasoning.
studies.abstract: Large-scale brain networks are integral to the coordination of human behaviour, and their anatomy provides insights into the clinical presentation and progression of neurodegenerative illnesses such as Alzheimer's disease, which targets the default mode network, and behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia, which targets a more anterior salience network. Although the default mode network is recruited when healthy subjects deliberate about 'personal' moral dilemmas, patients with Alzheimer's disease give normal responses to these dilemmas whereas patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia give abnormal responses to these dilemmas. We hypothesized that this apparent discrepancy between activation- and patient-based studies of moral reasoning might reflect a modulatory role for the salience network in regulating default mode network activation. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging to characterize network activity of patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia and healthy control subjects, we present four converging lines of evidence supporting a causal influence from the salience network to the default mode network during moral reasoning. First, as previously reported, the default mode network is recruited when healthy subjects deliberate about 'personal' moral dilemmas, but patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia producing atrophy in the salience network give abnormally utilitarian responses to these dilemmas. Second, patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia have reduced recruitment of the default mode network compared with healthy control subjects when deliberating about these dilemmas. Third, a Granger causality analysis of functional neuroimaging data from healthy control subjects demonstrates directed functional connectivity from nodes of the salience network to nodes of the default mode network during moral reasoning. Fourth, this Granger causal influence is diminished in patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia. These findings are consistent with a broader model in which the salience network modulates the activity of other large-scale networks, and suggest a revision to a previously proposed 'dual-process' account of moral reasoning. These findings also characterize network interactions underlying abnormal moral reasoning in frontotemporal dementia, which may serve as a model for the aberrant judgement and interpersonal behaviour observed in this disease and in other disorders of social function. More broadly, these findings link recent work on the dynamic interrelationships between large-scale brain networks to observable impairments in dementia syndromes, which may shed light on how diseases that target one network also alter the function of interrelated networks.

studies.title: Self-appraisal in behavioural variant frontotemporal degeneration.
studies.abstract: Previous work investigating deficits in self-appraisal in behavioural-variant frontotemporal degeneration (bvFTD) has focused on a single domain: social/behavioural processes. We examined whether a domain-specific versus multi-domain model best explains degraded self-appraisal in bvFTD.

studies.title: Face shape and face identity processing in behavioral variant fronto-temporal dementia: A specific deficit for familiarity and name recognition of famous faces.
studies.abstract: Deficits in face processing have been described in the behavioral variant of fronto-temporal dementia (bvFTD), primarily regarding the recognition of facial expressions. Less is known about face shape and face identity processing. Here we used a hierarchical strategy targeting face shape and face identity recognition in bvFTD and matched healthy controls. Participants performed 3 psychophysical experiments targeting face shape detection (Experiment 1), unfamiliar face identity matching (Experiment 2), familiarity categorization and famous face-name matching (Experiment 3). The results revealed group differences only in Experiment 3, with a deficit in the bvFTD group for both familiarity categorization and famous face-name matching. Voxel-based morphometry regression analyses in the bvFTD group revealed an association between grey matter volume of the left ventral anterior temporal lobe and familiarity recognition, while face-name matching correlated with grey matter volume of the bilateral ventral anterior temporal lobes. Subsequently, we quantified familiarity-specific and name-specific recognition deficits as the sum of the celebrities of which respectively only the name or only the familiarity was accurately recognized. Both indices were associated with grey matter volume of the bilateral anterior temporal cortices. These findings extent previous results by documenting the involvement of the left anterior temporal lobe (ATL) in familiarity detection and the right ATL in name recognition deficits in fronto-temporal lobar degeneration.

Imaging modality includes VBM (and FDG-PET performed in most patients). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients=23, controls=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and statistics), Results (behavior and imaging) and Discussion; core article content is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and the reporting allowance I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used VBM), I4 (cohort includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=22), I5 (patient group and healthy control group sizes >=6). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7. The paper does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that isolates the bvFTD group versus healthy controls in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates. VBM analyses reported are symptom-correlations within the combined FTLD cohort (and within the AD cohort) and regressions including syndromic group as a covariate, rather than a bvFTD vs control group-level voxelwise contrast. No bvFTD-specific whole-brain coordinate-based results are provided in the text or tables; therefore the study does not satisfy the requirement for bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses constrained to an a priori cortical midline structures (CMS) region-of-interest mask rather than reporting at least one whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result. Thus Exclusion E6 applies (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD n=22 and controls n=17, both ≥6), and I6 (reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with coordinates in MNI space). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no clear whole-brain voxelwise group-level result from the target sample). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study uses VBM (I3 satisfied), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=19) (I4 satisfied) and has adequate group sizes (bvFTD n=19; controls n=21) (I5 satisfied). However, the VBM analyses reported are within-patient-group voxelwise correlations of grey matter with behavioural/EMG measures rather than between-group voxelwise contrasts directly comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard space. Therefore it does not provide the required between-group (bvFTD vs controls) whole-brain voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach coordinates (I6 not met) nor a clear whole-brain group-level between-group result from the target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review’s target-sample criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET) and I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6: FTLD N=14, controls N=13). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — participants are described as ‘‘FTLD’’ (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specifying behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease, so the target diagnostic group (bvFTD/Pick’s) is not clearly present; I6 — there are no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (the paper used SVM classification and ROI coordinates drawn from prior meta-analyses rather than reporting new bvFTD-specific voxelwise coordinate contrasts); I7 — although whole-brain SVM weight maps are presented for FTLD vs. controls, they are not clearly identified as coming from a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD sample. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

While the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes (I5), it does not report a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The reported whole-brain VBM results are across a heterogeneous patient sample and the bvFTD-specific analyses are ROI-restricted to the insula. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

Study is EXCLUDED because it does not report a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (Inclusion criterion I6 not met). The paper performs within-group voxel-based morphometry correlations of reward-seeking scores in bvFTD patients (whole-brain VBM), but no group-level bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrasts are provided. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sample size >6: 103 patients, 91 imaged), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results from the target sample as within-group VBM), I8 (results reported in MNI coordinates/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study in PLOS ONE that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=27). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with MNI stereotaxic coordinates and figures; analyses were performed separately for bvFTD (not pooled with other FTD subtypes). The study also provides group-level whole-brain results (FWE-corrected atrophy maps and uncorrected voxelwise correlations reported with cluster extent) and presents coordinates in text/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, DTI/FC-only methods, or samples with disqualifying comorbidities) are violated. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=28) (I4), and meets sample-size requirements for patients and controls (I5), it does not present any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). The VBM results are regression-based across a pooled, mixed-diagnosis sample (polisher/neutral and tarnisher/neutral analyses) and do not report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results coming specifically from the bvFTD subgroup (I7 not met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study that reports voxelwise group contrasts with coordinates comparing FTD patients to controls. Imaging modality: VBM (meets I3). Sample: includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients meeting Neary criteria and behavioral descriptions consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (meets I4). Sample sizes exceed thresholds (32 patients total, 27 with usable MRI; 47 controls) satisfying I5. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (overeating FTD subgroup vs nonovereaters and controls) with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach reported), satisfying I6 and I8. VBM analyses are voxelwise/group-level whole-brain comparisons within an a priori ROI and results are clearly identified as coming from the target patient group (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not only FC/DTI/thickness, and no disqualifying comorbid sample issues). Note: the authors use the term “FTD” and Neary criteria rather than explicitly ‘bvFTD’; behavioral descriptions and diagnostic criteria indicate behavioral-variant FTD, which slightly reduces but does not preclude inclusion. Overall confidence 0.85.

This study used VBM (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13, I4), and had adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (bvFTD n=13; controls n=20, I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are correlational within a combined patient cohort and significant effects were reported only within pre-specified regions of interest; no between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) are presented, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI findings / no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This study reports FDG-PET (I3) on a clinically diagnosed frontal/behavioral variant FTD sample (bvFTD; I4). Imaging results are voxelwise SPM whole-brain analyses reported with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics comparing patient groups to healthy controls (satisfies I6, I7, I8). PET subgroup sizes meet the minimum (H1 N=31, H2 N=10, controls N=16), and whole-brain between-group contrasts (H1 vs controls, H2 vs controls, and H1 vs H2) are reported, with coordinates provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes a clinically diagnosed FTD subgroup (n=9) within an FTLD sample of 14 patients, and provides whole-brain voxelwise SPM results in stereotaxic space. However, it does NOT report a between-group contrast of bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) versus healthy controls, and the reported whole-brain results are for a pooled FTLD group (FTD, SD, PPA) compared to an EOAD patient group rather than isolated bvFTD vs controls. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within the FTD sample (17 bvFTD patients) satisfying the minimum sample-size requirements (I4, I5), the reported voxelwise whole-brain results are for the pooled FTD group (FTD = 52) and for AD vs controls. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts or coordinate results that are specific to the behavioral-variant FTD subgroup (bvFTD) alone. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and the requirement that at least one whole-brain result be clearly identified as coming from the target sample (I7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (FTD subgroup) (I4), has adequate sample sizes (17 patients, 9 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group analyses comparing FTD and SD to controls (unpooled FTD vs controls) (I6,I7). The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain results (BA labels and cluster reporting) and refers to tables/figures for coordinates, which satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on whole-brain T1-weighted MRI and reports voxelwise group comparisons with MNI coordinates. The ALS-FTD subgroup (n=18) met clinical Neary criteria for FTD and predominantly showed behavioral abnormalities consistent with bvFTD; neurologic disease controls (n=15) are included. VBM whole-brain results (voxelwise, corrected p<0.05) are reported for ALS-FTD versus controls and versus other ALS subgroups and coordinate tables (MNI) are provided. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patient and control groups ≥6). The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present; supplementary material being online is acceptable. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical VBM study that compares a clinically defined frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (behaviorally defined FTD; patients with predominant behavioral/frontal syndrome, excluding progressive aphasia/semantic dementia) to healthy controls using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The patient sample includes 9 FTD participants and 26 controls, meeting the minimum N≥6 for both groups (I5). Between-group voxelwise contrasts are reported in stereotactic space (SPM coordinates; e.g., periaqueductal gray at (0,-28,-10)) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are presented and attributed to the FTD sample (I6, I7). Results are reported as corrected and uncorrected voxelwise findings and coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria (reviews-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, DTI/FC/CTh-only, or prohibited comorbid-sample) are met. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the inclusion criteria: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included), I5 (patient group n=12 and control group n=12, both ≥6), I6 (reports between-group contrasts with stereotactic coordinates), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results reported), and I8 (results described in text/figures/tables). However, exclusion criterion E7 is met: the bvFTD sample includes patients with comorbid motor neuron disease (neurological symptoms) documented in the text (3/12 bvFTD), which violates the requirement to exclude samples with concurrent neurological disorders. Therefore the study must be excluded per the review rules. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study that directly investigates bvFTD. It uses voxel-based morphometry (FSL VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=25) (I4) and healthy controls (n=25) with adequate sample sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with results provided in stereotaxic space (MNI) and discusses voxelwise group-level findings (I6, I7, I8). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria were violated: this is not a review/meta-analysis (not E5), whole-brain results are reported (not E6), participants with psychiatric/other dementia/substance-abuse were explicitly excluded from recruitment (so E7 not met), it is empirical (not E8), and it does not report only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness (not E9). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study should be excluded because the imaging analysis reported is cortical thickness-based rather than one of the eligible modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). This meets exclusion criterion E9 (studies that report only cortical thickness methods). The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and controls), I6 (between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls reported), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise cortical-thickness results reported), and I8 (results referenced in tables/figures). However it fails I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclusion is based on E9 and failure to meet I3.

While the study uses voxel-based morphometry (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=12) with healthy controls (n=17) satisfying sample size requirements (I4, I5), it does not report a between-group, voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI/Talairach space. The neuroimaging results are voxelwise regressions of flavour identification across the patient cohort and associations within the bvFTD subgroup, but no explicit bvFTD vs control whole-brain between-group contrast is presented. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls) is not met, which is required for inclusion. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes an adequate sample size (18 patients, 17 controls) satisfying I5. The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases with frontal-variant/behavioural features (fvFTD), so participants with behavioural-variant presentations are present (I4). However, the paper does not report a between-group whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD (or fvFTD-only) group to controls that is not pooled with other FTD subtypes. The group-level VBM contrast reported is for a heterogeneous FTD group versus controls, and the behavioural analysis is a covariate correlation (NPI) across the mixed FTD cohort rather than a bvFTD-only voxelwise group contrast. Therefore criteria I6 and I7 are not met (no isolated bvFTD group whole-brain between-group result). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Exclusion is based on failing required inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This study reports voxelwise FDG-PET analyses in a sample of 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients (PPA and semantic dementia explicitly excluded), with age-matched controls. The methods use SPM in MNI space and report group-level, whole-brain results (conjunction and subtraction analyses) including MNI coordinates (e.g., 4,62,-6; Z=7.03). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (29 patients; controls per center ≥6). The analyses are whole-brain voxelwise (not ROI-only) and the bvFTD-like clinical phenotype (behavioral/social disinhibition, loss of insight) is consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: imaging modality is FDG-PET (I3); the sample comprises clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients per Lund–Manchester criteria with other FTLD variants (semantic dementia, non-fluent progressive aphasia) excluded, consistent with a behavioral-variant FTD sample (I4) — diagnosis based on clinical criteria and PET pattern; sample sizes meet minimums (29 patients, 16 controls) (I5); the paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing FTD to controls with coordinates reported in Talairach/MNI space (I6); whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM results are clearly identified as coming from the patient group (I7); results are reported as coordinates/figures and described in text (I8). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria were met.

This study used VBM and included bvFTD patients (N=23) but does not provide any between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls nor report whole-brain voxelwise results that are specifically from a bvFTD vs control contrast. Instead, VBM correlations are reported across a pooled sample of 75 neurodegeneration patients with diagnosis entered as covariates. Thus it fails to meet criteria requiring (I6) a bvFTD-specific between-group contrast and (I7) at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD participants included), I5 (bvFTD group size >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) versus healthy controls (n=11). It uses task fMRI (I3), includes a bvFTD sample (I4), and both patient and control groups exceed the minimum size of 6 participants (I5). The paper reports between-group contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI) comparing bvFTD to controls (I6) and presents at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) result with FWE whole-brain correction (I7). Reporting of coordinates/figures and text descriptions satisfy acceptable reporting (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is empirical original research, not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbid sample, and not limited to excluded modalities. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) and adequate control samples, but it does not report any voxelwise, between-group contrast that specifically compares a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls in stereotactic space. Instead, VBM analyses are reported for behavioral subgroups defined by storytelling characteristics (mixed diagnostic composition). Thus key inclusion criteria for this review are not met: no bvFTD-specific whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group results are provided. Exclusion criteria: none met.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (voxel-based morphometry) alongside DTI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=29) (I4), and has an adequate control group (n=37) and patient group sizes (>6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level VBM analyses and disease maps for the bvFTD group relative to controls using images in standard MNI space, with results summarized in figures/tables (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: it is an empirical study (not a review), includes whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and is not limited to only DTI/seed-based FC/cortical thickness methods. The provided full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and supplementary references to figures/tables).

This study uses VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (16 bvFTD within 26 FTLD patients) and 21 healthy controls, and the patient and control sample sizes meet minimum thresholds. However the imaging analyses reported are voxelwise regression associations between grey matter and emotion-recognition performance within a combined FTLD cohort (and VBM was performed on FTLD patients only). The paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls in standard stereotactic space, nor does it present bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This VBM study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with early prominent behavioural features consistent with bvFTD within the sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls), and I8 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures). However it does NOT meet key meta-analysis requirements: I6 and I7 are not satisfied because the paper does not report a between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group to healthy controls — instead analyses are performed on the mixed FTLD cohort (13 FTD + 3 SD) or on behavioural covariates within that pooled group. Therefore the target sample (bvFTD) is not isolated for a between-group voxelwise contrast, so the study cannot be included. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) .

This study is excluded because it does not provide results specific to the target clinical group (bvFTD). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient and control groups exceed 6 subjects), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not clearly report that participants are clinically-diagnosed bvFTD specifically; sample is mixed FTD phenotypes), I6 (no between-group contrast presented that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls in stereotactic space). Although whole-brain VBM analyses are reported for FTD and GRN+ vs GRN- comparisons, these are not specific to bvFTD and the bvFTD subgroup is neither isolated nor reported in coordinate-based contrasts. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5-E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. Imaging modality: voxel‑based morphometry (VBM) was used (I3). Sample: includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=23), meeting minimum group sizes (I4, I5). Whole‑brain, voxelwise VBM comparisons were performed between patient groups and controls (bvFTD vs controls reported) and between AD and bvFTD, with cluster-level results reported and corrected (whole‑brain evidence) (I6, I7). Results include MNI coordinates for at least some voxelwise findings and supplementary material is referenced, satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical, original VBM study (not a review), it reports whole‑brain analyses (not ROI‑only), and comorbidities/alcohol abuse were exclusionary in participant selection. Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM99 VBM) and includes a behavioral-variant-like subgroup (SOC/EXEC), with sufficient sample sizes (FTD-related n=73; controls n=13). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (voxelwise correlations of CSF tau with gray matter atrophy) in the FTD patient group. However, it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrast in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) directly comparing a bvFTD (SOC/EXEC) group to healthy controls where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. Inclusion criterion I6 (a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is therefore not met. Accordingly, the study must be excluded.

Excluded because the study does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise results specific to a bvFTD group (bvFTD subgroup = 5 subjects). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients were included in the sample), I5 (overall patient group n=15 and control group n=12 meet the >=6 requirement), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other FTD subtypes) and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E5–E9 apply). Because the meta-analysis objective targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts (unpooled bvFTD group) and this study only reports mixed-FTD contrasts or subgroup analyses where the bvFTD cell has n<6, it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the sample: 47 bvFTD), and I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=47, controls n=34, both ≥6). However it does NOT meet I6 and I7: the published whole-brain VBM results are correlational analyses within the combined FTD patient sample (atrophy correlated with happiness behavior) rather than a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. No group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group alone (bvFTD results are not presented as an independent between-group contrast vs controls). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s required target diagnosis. Although it uses FDG-PET (I3) and appears to have sufficient group sizes (I5), the patient sample is described as heterogeneous FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specification that participants were clinically diagnosed with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Consequently, the paper does not report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) group to controls (I6 and I7 are not satisfied for the target sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered by the full text. Summary: exclusion IDs met: none; inclusion IDs met: I3, I5; inclusion IDs not met: I4, I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM as imaging modality), I5 (FTD patient group n=29 and control group n=12, both ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group-level results in Talairach space). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper does not explicitly state inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD/bvFTD or Pick’s disease; FTD sample is described as heterogeneous subgroups including primary progressive aphasia and a subgroup with “disorder of social and executive functioning,” but bvFTD is not explicitly identified), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically for a bvFTD-only group versus controls; results are reported for the pooled FTD group). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are triggered. Because the review targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts, lack of an isolated bvFTD group/contrast prevents inclusion.

This study uses VBM and includes a clinically-diagnosed FTD subgroup with adequate sample size, but it does not report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts directly comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The VBM analyses are covariate-based regressions across a pooled sample (patients and controls) relating gray matter volume to music-task performance; results are presented as correlations with task scores rather than as group-level FTD vs control contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (explicit between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls; at least one group-level whole-brain result from the target sample) are not met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD with behavioral features consistent with bvFTD), I5 (patient and control group sizes meet the >=6 threshold). No exclusion criteria apply. Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study uses task-based fMRI (n-back) and includes 7 FTD patients, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results with Talairach coordinates (supplementary tables). However, it does not explicitly state that the patient sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not clearly met). Also, the between-group contrasts reported compare FTD to Alzheimer’s disease patients rather than to healthy controls; inclusion criterion I6 requires a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This FDG-PET study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients and meets imaging modality (I3), includes FTD (behavioral syndrome) patients (I4), and has sufficient patient numbers (I5). However, it does not report a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD (or FTD) to healthy controls: the main voxelwise comparisons are FTLD+UIC vs FTLD−UIC, and subgroup analyses restricted to FTD compare incontinent vs continent FTD patients (no healthy control group). Inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) and I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise result originating from a bvFTD vs control contrast) are not met. The FTD-restricted results did not survive correction and are reported only uncorrected, and the primary analyses pooled FTLD subtypes. Therefore it does not satisfy the review’s requirement for bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (n=12) (I4). Patient and control group sizes meet the >=6 requirement (FTD 12, controls 10) (I5). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group comparisons in MNI space with coordinates and cluster information comparing bvFTD to controls (I6, I7), and results are presented in figures/tables/supplementary material (I8). It is not a review, does not report only ROI analyses, and does not use excluded modalities only, so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within FTLD sample), I5 (patient group N=37, >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing a bvFTD group versus healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space—the VBM contrasts compare musicophilic vs non-musicophilic FTLD subgroups, not bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). Exclusion criteria: none met. Therefore exclude because the study does not provide the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain between-group contrasts (I6/I7).

Study uses FDG-PET (I3 satisfied). However it does not provide data specific to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease: the FTLD group includes 13 patients with only 3 labelled as 'FTD' (not specified as bvFTD), so there is no distinct bvFTD group (I4 not met). The bvFTD-relevant subgroup size is <6 (FTD n=3), so the sample-size criterion for the target group is not met (I5 not met). The reported between-group voxelwise contrasts are for aggregated FTLD (vs subjective cognitive impairment) rather than a bvFTD group unpooled from other diagnoses, so there is no between-group contrast specific to bvFTD (I6 not met) and no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study uses VBM (I3 satisfied), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD participants (bvFTD n=21; I4 satisfied), and meets the sample size requirement (≥6 bvFTD patients; I5 satisfied). However, the paper does not clearly report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) that compares an isolated bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to healthy controls in the main text. While the authors state that VBM analyses of FTLD subgroups versus healthy controls are presented in the Supplementary material, the full text does not explicitly present a bvFTD versus control whole-brain coordinate-based contrast clearly attributable to the bvFTD group alone. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met from the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text is complete. This fMRI resting-state study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including 18 bvFTD cases) and reports whole-brain voxelwise ICA results correlating Reserve Index with functional connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases), I5 (patient subgroup size ≥6), I8 (results reported with MNI coordinates/voxelwise clusters). However, it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (bvFTD results are not presented as a distinct between-group contrast against controls). Consequently I7 is not met for the target comparison: there are no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD vs control contrast. Because both I6 and I7 are required, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (FTLD/FTD vs controls) with coordinates in standardized space (MNI) and corrected results, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements (I6,I7,I8). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD (behavioral variant/frontotemporal dementia) as a distinct subgroup (FTD n=15) within FTLD (I4), with adequate group sizes (FTLD n=25 total; VBM available in 21 FTLD and 17 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, VBM analyses and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered: this is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and it does not use excluded modalities. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E6 applied: the study reports VBM analyses but finds no significant whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level results and instead reports only small-volume (region-of-interest) corrected findings and voxelwise correlations within the patient groups. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=22), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group directly to controls—analyses focus on correlations within patients and combined patient cohorts rather than bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no significant group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported for the target group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain, between-group voxelwise results and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used FDG-PET), I5 (FTD patient group n=10 and healthy control group n=46 meet minimum sample sizes), I7 (voxelwise, whole-brain SPM group-level contrasts are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the paper does not report between-group contrast results in a defined stereotactic coordinate space such as MNI or Talairach; no coordinate tables or explicit stereotactic coordinates are provided in the full text), I4 (the clinical sample is described as frontotemporal dementia per Lund and Manchester criteria but the paper does not explicitly state 'behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD)' or Pick's disease; vagueness about variant undermines certainty that target diagnosis is bvFTD). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were directly violated. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Given failure to satisfy I6 (and uncertainty about I4), the study must be excluded from the bvFTD meta-analysis.

The study used FDG-PET (I3) and included >6 FTD patients and >6 controls (I5). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD subtypes, including behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4). However, it does NOT report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls (I6 not met). The reported PET result is a voxelwise correlation of metabolic rate with prosocial sexual behavior across combined patient groups (FTD and CBS), not a bvFTD vs control group-level contrast, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result is clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only group (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

Included imaging modality and samples: this study uses voxel-based morphometry (satisfies I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (11 patients) (satisfies I4), and has adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=11; controls n=22) (satisfies I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are associations across the combined patient cohort (AD, bvFTD, SD, PNFA) and regression-based correlations with musical performance; the paper does not present a voxelwise between-group contrast in standard space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group specifically to controls unpooled (I6 not met). Consequently, there is no clear group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) result identified as coming from the bvFTD sample alone (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7.

This study is excluded because, although it uses VBM (I3) and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s patients (I4), it does not report a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled with other FTD subtypes) to controls in stereotactic coordinates. Thus it fails I6 and I7. The bvFTD subgroup sample size for a standalone bvFTD vs control contrast is not reported clearly, so I5 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (7/14; meets I4), has adequate group sizes (FTD n=14, controls n≥6; meets I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates/figures in MNI space (meets I7 and I8). However, all reported between-group analyses compare the combined FTD-GRN+ group (which mixes bvFTD and avPPA cases) to controls; the paper does not present a bvFTD-only versus controls whole-brain contrast (i.e., the bvFTD group is pooled with other patients). Therefore it fails to meet I6, which requires between-group contrasts where the bvFTD group is not pooled. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet I6.

The study used FDG-PET and SPM5 and included an FTD patient group (n=7) with healthy controls (n=18), so imaging modality (I3) and sample size (I5) criteria are met. However, the paper reports results for a general FTD group without specifying behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; inclusion criterion I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease) is not satisfied. Consequently, criteria that require bvFTD-specific between-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain results (I6, I7, I8) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not specifically report on bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses relating gray matter atrophy to speech fluency in FTLD subgroups. The cohort includes a social/executive (SOC/EXEC) subgroup characterized by social comportment and executive deficits consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. Imaging was performed on a subset (n=22 patients; SOC/EXEC n=9) and contrasted against age-matched controls (n=31) using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses in MNI space; subgroup-specific atrophy maps and overlaps with fluency-related voxels are reported in figures and tables. Sample sizes meet the >=6 patient and >=6 control thresholds for the SOC/EXEC imaging subgroup. Thus the study provides whole-brain, between-group VBM results for a bvFTD-like group. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis, review article, disallowed modality) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendices).

Study uses VBM and includes bvFTD patients (11 bvFTD) with adequate sample sizes and reports voxelwise MNI coordinates for associations; however it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group alone to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. VBM analyses were performed as correlations within the combined FTLD patient cohort (and significant inference was made using small-volume correction within pre-specified ROIs). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4 and I5 are met, but I6 and I7 (require a between-group contrast in stereotactic space for the bvFTD group and at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample) are not met. Additionally, the reported neuroimaging inference relied on small-volume/ROI correction rather than whole-brain group-level results, invoking exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an original empirical study that used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with MNI coordinates and tract-based spatial statistics. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=14), both exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the bvFTD group versus controls with MNI coordinates and presents group-level, whole-brain results in text/figures. The full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (FSL-VBM) and provides group-level, voxelwise contrasts comparing patient groups to healthy controls with MNI coordinates and figures/tables. The sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (n=10) and healthy controls (n=14), meeting the minimum N≥6 requirement. The paper reports between-group VBM contrasts for bvFTD versus controls and covariate analyses (age, comprehension) with whole-brain results clearly attributed to the bvFTD group. Imaging modality, sample, sample size, voxelwise whole-brain reporting, and coordinate reporting criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; no disqualifying comorbidities reported; empirical study; not solely FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (and TBSS/DTI) as imaging modalities and explicitly included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=10) and healthy controls (n=26). The bvFTD patient group meets the minimum sample size requirement (>=6) and controls also exceed the minimum (>=6). The paper reports that separate VBM group-level analyses were run for each patient group (including bvFTD) versus healthy controls and refers to results/coordinates reported in the Supplementary Information (S11), satisfying the requirement for at least one between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast in stereotactic space. Whole-brain VBM and TBSS results (with cluster/peak reporting and FWE-corrected thresholds) are described in the text and figures, and the authors note coordinates/peaks and use standard MNI space. Supplementary materials are acceptable per inclusion rules. Given these points, the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis. Confidence is somewhat reduced because some between-group coordinate tables are reported in Supplementary Information rather than the main text, but the manuscript clearly indicates those whole-brain contrasts were performed and reported.

This study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (satisfies I3) and includes sufficient participant numbers across patient and control groups (satisfies I5). However, it does not report results specifically for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease patients: the sample lists participants with “frontotemporal dementia (FTD)” but does not specify behavioral-variant FTD or provide a bvFTD-only group (I4 not met). Consequently, there are no between-group whole-brain contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met), and no group-level whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet I4, I6, and I7.

Study uses VBM and includes a clinically defined FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=47) and healthy controls (n=43), meeting imaging and sample-size criteria. However, the neuroimaging analyses report whole-brain voxelwise correlations of interpersonal traits across a mixed diagnostic sample and co-atrophy checks; the paper does not present any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast or group-level VBM result specifically comparing the bvFTD (FTD variant) group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 (bvFTD-specific between-group, whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Excluded on the basis of missing bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group results.

The full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM structural MRI), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, N=31), I5 (patient and control groups each ≥6; bvFTD N=31, controls N=75). Not met: I6 and I7 — the paper does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing bvFTD vs healthy controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The primary VBM results are covariate-only regressions of BIS/BAS scores across the pooled sample and correlations that span diagnostic groups; co-atrophy checks control for diagnosis but no direct group-level bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control voxelwise contrast is presented. No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., it is not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level whole-brain bvFTD vs control result and must be excluded.

This study meets several inclusion criteria for the review: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients consistent with behavioral-variant FTD), I5 (sufficient sample sizes: FTD n=30; controls n=20), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the FTD subgroup in diagnostic subgroup interaction analyses), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures). However, it fails to meet I6: the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast in standard (MNI/Talairach) space directly comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to healthy controls (the authors explicitly state that normal controls were not used for any VBM analysis). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks the required bvFTD vs control whole-brain between-group contrast (I6 not met).

The full text reports empirical neuroimaging data in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD cohort using voxel-based morphometry and task-based fMRI (satisfies I3). The sample includes >6 bvFTD patients (10 behavioral analyses, 8 in neuroimaging) and 16 controls (satisfies I4 and I5). The paper reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (VBM and fMRI) comparing bvFTD patients to controls, with results presented in tables/figures and coordinates (satisfies I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review/meta-analysis, includes whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not report only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness; there is no indication of comorbid psychiatric diagnoses or other dementia pooling that would violate E7. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key bvFTD-specific inclusion criteria. Although it uses VBM (I3 satisfied) and has adequate group sizes (FTD n=9, controls n=10; I5 satisfied), it does not include a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group explicitly (I4 not met). The VBM analysis was a covariate-only correlation across all diagnostic groups rather than a between-group, voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met) and therefore does not provide whole-brain group-level results from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered.

This is an empirical VBM study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons involving a clearly defined bvFTD group. The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM5) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=49) (I4) and an age-matched healthy control group (n=30) satisfying the minimum sample-size requirement (I5). The manuscript reports between-group whole-brain contrasts and voxelwise regression results, with peak coordinates converted to Talairach space (I6,I7,I8). The full text contains introduction, methods (neuropsychology and structural imaging), results (including tables/figures of atrophy and regressions), and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (23 patients included) with a healthy control group (20 controls). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons (two-sample t-test) showing atrophic clusters in bilateral anterior temporal lobes and additional regions, and voxelwise regression analyses relating behavioral measures to GM volume in the patient group. Imaging modality includes VBM (and FDG-PET performed in most patients). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients=23, controls=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and statistics), Results (behavior and imaging) and Discussion; core article content is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and the reporting allowance I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=20) and healthy controls (n=13), but it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI/Talairach space. The reported VBM analyses are correlational across a mixed diagnostic sample and regression analyses controlling for diagnosis, not a group-level bvFTD vs control coordinate-based contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7.
